The ruling has been hailed as a significant moment for justice, eliciting emotional responses from the Rohingya community and advocates worldwide. The move aims to facilitate the return of migrants without legal residency in Europe, although it is expected to face legal challenges and criticism from human rights groups.

Described as the first initiative of its kind outside the EU, the centre is intended to provide an alternative for people who cannot in practice be returned to their countries of origin. The countries and Rwanda will now develop the model with international organisations, with the governments aiming for initial transfers in 2027.

Nine victims—six men and three women—were found shot dead in a shack in Jeffsville, Atteridgeville, near Pretoria, while eight men were found dead in a vehicle in Sweetwaters near Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal. Police launched investigations in both provinces, deploying specialist units in Gauteng and collecting evidence at the KwaZulu-Natal scene. No arrests or suspects had been publicly announced.
